- Overestimate prices when sentiment is negative or mildly bearish (especially after recent spikes); reduce forecast peak values.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is strongly positive or volatile; increase baseline forecast slightly.
- Overshoot after sharp upward moves; cap forecast peaks at 1–2% below true high if sentiment turns negative.
- Lagged corrections: if sentiment turns bearish after a forecast peak, reduce next 3–5 days’ forecast by 0.5–1.5%.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, adjust downward by 0.5–1.0% per day until convergence.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts overestimate when sentiment is weak or trending sideways; reduce by 0.5–1.5% if sentiment < 0.10 for 3+ days.
- Avoid overreacting to single-day sentiment spikes; smooth forecasts with 3-day moving average if sentiment volatility > 0.30.
